**Explanation:** 
The ending of the story feels natural, earned, and purposeful rather than abrupt or arbitrary. It successfully resolves the central conflict—the three-year struggle to waterproof the building and protect the endangered-language archive—when Dr. Amsel listens to the autumn storm and hears the new roof holding the water back. Furthermore, the conclusion weaves together the recurring motifs and themes introduced throughout the piece, such as the linguistics of weather, institutional bureaucracy ("phases" and "pending final budget approval"), and Mrs. Blythe's index cards. The emotional arc of the faculty also reaches a satisfying resolution, shifting from frustration to a shared, resilient camaraderie and cautious hope for the future.
